the-revenant-2015.author: Jaime N. Christley

dont-look-up.quote: Don’t Look Up might be the funniest movie of 2021. It’s the most depressing too, and that odd combination makes for a one-of-a-kind experience. Writer-director Adam McKay gives you over two hours of laughs while convincing you that the world is coming to an end.
dont-look-up.author: Mick LaSalle

dont-look-up.quote: Don’t Look Up takes the pulse of contemporary life and finds it crazy, scary and, most of all, funny. It doesn’t all land but enough does to make it a sharp, bold, star-studded treat.
dont-look-up.author: Ian Freer

dont-look-up.quote: Don’t Look Up is a deeply unsettling yet darkly humorous watch. It has just the right amount of comedy and zeal without losing sight of its message or the tension bubbling beneath the surface.
dont-look-up.author: Mae Abdulbaki

dont-look-up.quote: There’s something oddly satisfying about the way McKay's film lets us laugh at our own doom.
dont-look-up.author: Clarisse Loughrey

dont-look-up.quote: Performances pop as Earth gets the chop, with US politics, big business and social media going up in flames.
dont-look-up.author: Jamie Graham

dont-look-up.quote: Fortunately, the core cast is phenomenal, especially leads DiCaprio and Lawrence, who are both luminous and effortless. Combine that with the fantastic editing and the jaw-dropping ending, and one gets a flawed but entirely worthwhile viewing experience.
dont-look-up.author: Bobby LePire

dont-look-up.quote: Frankly, it's almost enough just to watch them all run around in states that range from manic panic to Zen serenity while McKay employs his usual coterie of meta tricks and treats. But it's hard not to long for the shrewder movie that might have been: Not just a kooky scattershot look, but a deeper truer gaze into the void.
dont-look-up.author: Leah Greenblatt

dont-look-up.quote: If McKay crafted the most enjoyable parts of his satire with a scalpel, somebody should’ve handed him a machete to chop the script down some. The film clocks in at nearly two hours and 10 minutes, and we grow exhausted by it as the surprises stop and the ending becomes inevitable.
dont-look-up.author: Johnny Oleksinski

dont-look-up.quote: Not content with simply stoking rage and self-righteous superiority, McKay dares to infuse Don’t Look Up with an authentic, unironic sense of grief.
dont-look-up.author: Ann Hornaday

dont-look-up.quote: This is a stunningly accurate portrayal of our current climate. And it’s not pretty.
dont-look-up.author: Bill Goodykoontz

dont-look-up.quote: If it bears the fault of preaching to the choir’s anger more than offering real structural critique, one has to begrudgingly admire some qualities of his newest film, even as being annoyed for a good portion of the runtime is still expected.
dont-look-up.author: Ethan Vestby

dont-look-up.quote: Don’t Look Up is a strong idea (with story credit to McKay and journalist David Sirota), and lots of the individual jokes work, but at times it gets so caught up trying to make fun of so many different things that it seems to lack an internal logic. Satire in and of itself isn’t quite a story.
dont-look-up.author: Vince Mancini

dont-look-up.quote: Conceived as a climate-change metaphor, but given an oily new layer thanks to the pandemic, the film’s conceit could be sharply effective, in careful hands. But McKay knows only of punching down with meaty fists, so the result is a messy, smarmy assault.
dont-look-up.author: Barry Hertz

dont-look-up.quote: From Streep and DiCaprio and Lawrence through the supporting players, Don’t Look Up is filled with greatly talented actors really and truly selling this material — but the volume remains at 11 throughout the story when some changes in tone here and there might have more effectively carried the day.
dont-look-up.author: Richard Roeper

dont-look-up.quote: That the comet is a stand-in for climate change is hardly a secret going into Don’t Look Up, Adam McKay’s exceedingly watchable, funny and star-studded yet somewhat chaotic satire.
dont-look-up.author: Jocelyn Noveck

dont-look-up.quote: It all feels a little toothless.
dont-look-up.author: Hannah Strong

dont-look-up.quote: There are decent jokes all the way through, but, even at a groaning 145 minutes, the film feels overstuffed.
dont-look-up.author: Donald Clarke

dont-look-up.quote: Don’t Look Up’s driving thesis – roughly, “look at all these morons!” – is so basic it’s only really possible to respond to it as a hit-and-miss actors’ showcase.
dont-look-up.author: Tim Robey

dont-look-up.quote: McKay has a point, though his frame of reference hardly stretches beyond the United States, and the stink of localized political contempt all but overpowers the plot.
dont-look-up.author: Anthony Lane

dont-look-up.quote: McKay has made “Don’t Look Up,” a very angry, deeply anguished comedy freak out about how we are blowing it, hurtling toward oblivion. He’s sweetened the bummer setup with plenty of yuks — good, bad, indifferent — but if you weep, it may not be from laughing.
dont-look-up.author: Manohla Dargis

dont-look-up.quote: The satire of Don’t Look Up is anguished and clear to the point of feeling bludgeoning.
dont-look-up.author: David Sims

dont-look-up.quote: Don’t Look Up is both types of blunt: It makes no bones about exactly what the filmmakers think of climate-change deniers and social-media distractions, and it repeatedly blunts the impact of its satire by calling its shots early, often, and loudly.
dont-look-up.author: Jesse Hassenger

dont-look-up.quote: If you cherrypick the good stuff from a sea of unfocused choices, McKay’s all-star comedy (Leo! JLaw! Meryl!) about impending doom has its playful and provocative pleasures. But the laughs don’t stick in the throat the way they must in a screwball farce that ends in utter hopelessness.
dont-look-up.author: Peter Travers

dont-look-up.quote: Like Vice before it, the film too often uses satire as a tool of castigation rather than as a means of truly attacking the status quo.
dont-look-up.author: Derek Smith

dont-look-up.quote: In a grand science fiction tradition, Don't Look Up uses a disaster-movie framework as a metaphor for a reality-based crisis, with a huge comet hurtling toward Earth as a surrogate for indifference to addressing climate change. Yet this star-studded, extremely provocative satire at times veers off course itself, partially undermining its admirable qualities with the broadness of its tone.
dont-look-up.author: Brian Lowry

dont-look-up.quote: Nothing about the foolishness and outrageousness of what the movie shows us — no matter how virtuosically sliced and diced by McKay’s characteristically jittery editor, Hank Corwin — can really compete with the horrors of our real-world American idiocracy.
dont-look-up.author: Justin Chang

dont-look-up.quote: Where Don’t Look Up finds its strength is in its lead performances, which can’t be undone even by the film’s exhausting, rapid-fire editing and McKay’s aggressive indicating toward his own punchlines.
dont-look-up.author: Richard Lawson

dont-look-up.quote: Flat-footed and far too broad, it’s a reminder why “Saturday Night Live” skits don’t run two hours and 18 minutes.
dont-look-up.author: Mark Feeney

dont-look-up.quote: McKay keeps piling on the sardonic observations, and the outlandishly ill-behaved characters, long after the movie has crumpled under their weight.
dont-look-up.author: Stephanie Zacharek

dont-look-up.quote: McKay’s just as “right” about his target as ever. But the tone of this “Deep Impact/Wag the Dog” mashup is off. It veers towards strident, and as the clutter gathers around it, it drifts into dull. The jokes dry up and only a few members of his cast are veterans of “let make this funnier on the set” filmmaking.
dont-look-up.author: Roger Moore

dont-look-up.quote: For me, the bludgeoning tends to blunt the entertainment value.
dont-look-up.author: Alissa Wilkinson

dont-look-up.quote: With a generic cast, Don’t Look Up would have been a disappointment. With this star-studded cast, the classification of a “missed opportunity” doesn’t do it justice; it feels closer to a tragedy.
dont-look-up.author: James Berardinelli

dont-look-up.quote: The failure of topicality in “Don’t Look Up” is, not least, that the movie’s cynically apolitical view of politics contributes to the frivolous and self-regarding media environment that it decries—starting with the very celebrity power that the movie marshalls to score its points.
dont-look-up.author: Richard Brody

dont-look-up.quote: As is, Don’t Look Up is an exhausting and meandering “What if? But also, what now?” If the world really is going to end in my lifetime, these were 145 minutes that I’m never getting back.
dont-look-up.author: Brianna Zigler

dont-look-up.quote: And so we’re left with a very sweaty film that strains to be funny, but one that’s also itching to argue that it’s lack of funniness is precisely the point. Some problems can’t be solved by celebrities alone, and the most subversive thing about “Don’t Look Up” is ultimately how — in its own impotent way — it weaponizes its wild star power to make that point.
dont-look-up.author: David Ehrlich

dont-look-up.quote: The biggest problem with McKay’s stuff is that he thinks he’s the next Paddy Chayefsky, bringing down untold wisdom from on high and proclaiming disdain at the blinkered, media-soaked vagaries of our world. Unfortunately, he’s bought too deeply into his hype as a vivid truth-teller of society’s ills, and that smugness has infected too much of his films’ fabric.
dont-look-up.author: Clint Worthington

dont-look-up.quote: Running a long 145 minutes, it’s bleakly cartoonish polemic with few laughs or dramatic peaks, despite a climactic mad-as-hell speech from DiCaprio, some ineffectual pantomiming from Streep, and some third-act forced solemnity.
dont-look-up.author: Liam Lacey

dont-look-up.quote: This film could have done something more convincing with that mode of reverse-vertigo hinted at in its title: that fear and willed blindness about what looms over us. But if the movie helps to do something about climate change, such critical objections are unimportant.
dont-look-up.author: Peter Bradshaw

dont-look-up.quote: Worst of all, these final moments of the film make it abundantly clear that as a storyteller and a filmmaker, McKay has absolutely nothing to say about the topics he's skewering, and he shouldn't have even bothered to try. This is a hollow waste of time and talent; a comedy whose idea of humor is simply pointing a finger at something and chuckling obnoxiously. We, as a society, don't just deserve better leaders. We deserve better satire, too.
dont-look-up.author: Chris Evangelista

dont-look-up.quote: Clearly a commentary on global warming, which folds neatly into a treatise on our ongoing Covid-19 crisis, Don’t Look Up takes aim at plenty of ills — especially the scourge of science-deniers. But a smug, self-satisfied approach proves insufficient at addressing the legitimate woes at core of  this picture.
dont-look-up.author: Tim Grierson

dont-look-up.quote: I’d be hard-pressed to find a filmmaker who, in a general sense, I agree with but whose movies irritate me in the way that Adam McKay’s do.
dont-look-up.author: Trace Sauveur

dont-look-up.quote: It’s hard to think about who, exactly, is going to be moved to make changes to how they live their lives by Don’t Look Up, a climate-change allegory that acquired accidental COVID-19 relevance, but that doesn’t really end up being about much at all, beyond that humanity sucks.
dont-look-up.author: Alison Willmore

dont-look-up.quote: Humor is subjective, but giving an example of Don’t Look Up’s specific jokes feels like a spoiler, depriving you of one of the three times you’ll likely experience a genuine laugh.
dont-look-up.author: Joshua Rivera

dont-look-up.quote: The smug asides plastered on screen, and the hyperactive inserts of nature documentary footage do nothing to raise the film’s real-life stakes.
dont-look-up.author: Simran Hans

dont-look-up.quote: A disastrous movie, Don’t Look Up shows McKay as the most out of touch he’s ever been with what is clever, or how to get his audience to care.
dont-look-up.author: Nick Allen

dont-look-up.quote: The comic setups take longer than they should, then the punchlines give you a violent bear hug when they should be lightly slapping you on the cheek before quickly moving on to the next gag.
dont-look-up.author: Josh Larsen

dont-look-up.quote: It’s cheap, and crass, and by the conclusion, downright infuriating.
dont-look-up.author: Jason Bailey

dont-look-up.quote: Don’t Look Up plays like the leftie answer to “Armageddon” — which is to say, it ditches the Bruckheimer approach of assembling a bunch of blue-collar heroes to rocket out to space and nuke the approaching comet, opting instead to spotlight the apathy, incompetence and financial self-interest of all involved.
dont-look-up.author: Peter Debruge

dont-look-up.quote: A cynical, insufferably smug satire stuffed to the gills with stars that purports to comment on political and media inattention to the climate crisis but really just trivializes it. Dr. Strangelove it ain’t.
dont-look-up.author: David Rooney

dont-look-up.quote: A plausible premise, right? Yes, absolutely, but it’s squandered in a slapdash, scattershot sendup that turns almost everyone into nincompoops, trivializes everything it touches, oozes with self-delight, and becomes part of the babble and yammer it portrays.
dont-look-up.author: Joe Morgenstern

dont-look-up.quote: It’s a disaster movie in more ways than one. Should you indeed look up, you may be surprised to find one A-list bomb of a movie, all inchoate rage and flailing limbs, falling right on top of you.
dont-look-up.author: David Fear

dont-look-up.quote: A film with all the right things to say about how government, the media, and corporations ignore the emerging disaster of climate change, but couched within a satire so lumbering that it’s enough to turn a tree hugger into a pro-fracker.
dont-look-up.author: Alonso Duralde

there-will-be-blood.quote: There Will Be Blood is ferocious, and it will be championed and attacked with an equal ferocity. When the dust settles, we may look back on it as some kind of obsessed classic.
there-will-be-blood.author: David Ansen

there-will-be-blood.quote: There Will Be Blood is, in fact, not a historical saga; rather, it's an absurdist, blackly comic horror film with a very idiosyncratic satanic figure at its core.
there-will-be-blood.author: Glenn Kenny

there-will-be-blood.quote: Daniel Day-Lewis stuns in Paul Thomas Anderson's saga of a soul-dead oil man.
there-will-be-blood.author: John DeFore

there-will-be-blood.quote: An enthralling and powerfully eccentric American epic.
there-will-be-blood.author: David Denby

there-will-be-blood.quote: Boldly and magnificently strange, There Will Be Blood marks a significant departure in the work of Paul Thomas Anderson.
there-will-be-blood.author: Todd McCarthy

there-will-be-blood.quote: For a story that's all about the harnessing of fateful chthonic forces, Paul Thomas Anderson has dug deeper than ever before, and struck black gold.
there-will-be-blood.author: Dana Stevens

there-will-be-blood.quote: For bleakness, the movie can't be beat -- nor for brilliance.
there-will-be-blood.author: Lisa Schwarzbaum

there-will-be-blood.quote: The film is above all a consummate work of art, one that transcends the historically fraught context of its making, and its pleasures are unapologetically aesthetic. It reveals, excites, disturbs, provokes, but the window it opens is to human consciousness itself.
there-will-be-blood.author: Manohla Dargis

there-will-be-blood.quote: With There Will Be Blood, Paul Thomas Anderson has taken a stab at making The Great American Movie -- and I daresay he’s made one of them.
there-will-be-blood.author: Scott Foundas

there-will-be-blood.quote: This may be an extremely bold statement to make, but there hasn’t been such an amazing character study in film since “Citizen Kane.” I honestly can’t praise it enough. From the opening to the ghastly ending, this film will sit in the depths of your stomach for some time to come.
there-will-be-blood.author: Zack Haddad

there-will-be-blood.quote: This is truly a work of symphonic aspirations and masterful execution.
there-will-be-blood.author: J. Hoberman

there-will-be-blood.quote: Daniel Day-Lewis's portrayal is not just the performance of the year -- there will be injustice if he doesn't win an Oscar -- but a creation of awesome proportions.
there-will-be-blood.author: Joe Morgenstern

there-will-be-blood.quote: Anderson's uncompromising masterpiece will continue to resonate as a harrowing cautionary warning to a country with oil pumping through its veins, clouding its judgment and coarsening its soul.
there-will-be-blood.author: Nathan Rabin

there-will-be-blood.quote: One of the most wholly original American movies ever made.
there-will-be-blood.author: Richard Schickel

there-will-be-blood.quote: Day-Lewis... the role of a lifetime.
there-will-be-blood.author: Michael Phillips

there-will-be-blood.quote: A searing, apocalyptic and finally breathtaking drama.
there-will-be-blood.author: Ann Hornaday

there-will-be-blood.quote: An unusual, visually hypnotic, American Gothic historical epic that traces the rise and tragic fall of a Western mining magnate of the Gilded Age.
there-will-be-blood.author: William Arnold

there-will-be-blood.quote: There Will Be Blood" is anti-state of the art. It's the work of an analog filmmaker railing against an increasingly digitized world. In that sense, the movie is idiosyncratic, too: vintage visionary stuff.
there-will-be-blood.author: Wesley Morris

there-will-be-blood.quote: Anderson’s fearless, bighearted filmmaking is an antidote to the toxic cloud of Manifest Destiny. He has made a mad American classic.
there-will-be-blood.author: David Edelstein

there-will-be-blood.quote: In terms of excitement, imagination and rule-busting experimentation, it's a gusher.
there-will-be-blood.author: Peter Travers

there-will-be-blood.quote: The fact that that character happens to be so repellent -- and yet so endlessly fascinating -- is one of the film's many strokes of genius.
there-will-be-blood.author: Rene Rodriguez

there-will-be-blood.quote: There Will Be Blood is not a movie that disappears quietly.
there-will-be-blood.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

there-will-be-blood.quote: Uncompromising, intelligent and searing cinema. Along with The Assassination Of Jesse James... and No Country For Old Men, this is the best batch of Western-set dramas in decades. John Huston would have been proud.
there-will-be-blood.author: Helen O'Hara

there-will-be-blood.quote: This is a dark, uncompromising film, thrillingly original and distinctive, with a visionary passion. It is a movie against which all directors, and all moviegoers, will want to measure themselves.
there-will-be-blood.author: Peter Bradshaw

there-will-be-blood.quote: There Will Be Blood is a masterpiece; Daniel Day-Lewis' performance as a ruthless oilman is without flaw.
there-will-be-blood.author: Bill Goodykoontz

there-will-be-blood.quote: That Anderson, the film’s writer-director, whose Boogie Nights was a riot but Magnolia and Punch-Drunk Love both noble failures, has come to make this intelligent and enthralling masterpiece is both a little surprising and intensely satisfying.
there-will-be-blood.author: Dave Calhoun

there-will-be-blood.quote: Sprawling yet cramped, There Will Be Blood may not be the best movie of the year, but it's certainly the strangest. It evokes passing comparisons to everything from "Giant" to "Citizen Kane" but it's impossible to pigeonhole.
there-will-be-blood.author: Peter Rainer

there-will-be-blood.quote: It's first-rank filmmaking, through and through, even if it struggles to find closure.
there-will-be-blood.author: Shawn Levy

there-will-be-blood.quote: It's important to remember that Sinclair was as much a committed socialist as a novelist, someone who probably wrote for political purpose more than for dramatic effect. So while Day-Lewis' gorgeous acting largely disguises it, the people in "Blood" tend to be schematic and the film as a whole has a weakness for the didactic.
there-will-be-blood.author: Kenneth Turan

there-will-be-blood.quote: With a grating symphonic score by ­Radiohead's Jonny Greenwood and the constant sense of danger following Plainview, "Blood" does not release its grip on the audience until its last, bizarrely crazy minutes.
there-will-be-blood.author: Jack Mathews

there-will-be-blood.quote: Between D-Day, the sheer ambition of Paul Thomas Anderson's historical epic and Robert Elswit's dazzling cinematography, this is a must-see movie - even though its emotional temperature rarely rises above freezing and the climax goes way, way, way over the top.
there-will-be-blood.author: Lou Lumenick

there-will-be-blood.quote: A searingly intense and artful tale that grabs hold of the viewer from its jarring and wordless opening scenes and doesn't let go.
there-will-be-blood.author: Claudia Puig

there-will-be-blood.quote: The kind of film that is easily called great. I am not sure of its greatness. It was filmed in the same area of Texas used by "No Country for Old Men," and that is a great film, and a perfect one. But There Will Be Blood"is not perfect, and in its imperfections we may see its reach exceeding its grasp. Which is not a dishonorable thing.
there-will-be-blood.author: Roger Ebert

there-will-be-blood.quote: That's not to say that There Will Be Blood isn't something exceptional; it's just that the movie is jarringly erratic, ranging from moments of delicacy to majesty to over-the-top bombast.
there-will-be-blood.author: Liam Lacey

there-will-be-blood.quote: Just a few barrels short of being a masterpiece.
there-will-be-blood.author: Steven Rea

there-will-be-blood.quote: Ambitious, deeply flawed and studded with sequences that achieve pure, majestic greatness.
there-will-be-blood.author: Maitland McDonagh

there-will-be-blood.quote: Unfortunately, the film's final third is poorly focused and, while there is a clear conclusion, it feels strangely hollow.
there-will-be-blood.author: James Berardinelli

there-will-be-blood.quote: It's mostly a disturbingly believable portrait of a psychopath whose true depths of rage are buried where none but he can see. The ironically named Plainview does not come into plain view until the last scene, and the lupine, scowling Day-Lewis is mesmerizing in the role.
there-will-be-blood.author: Lawrence Toppman

there-will-be-blood.quote: This has loads of swagger, but for stylistic audacity I prefer Anderson's more scattershot "Magnolia."
there-will-be-blood.author: Jonathan Rosenbaum

there-will-be-blood.quote: There are epic impulses everywhere you look in There Will Be Blood; what's missing is character development, focused storytelling and, most significantly (apart from that terrific opening sequence), any sense of raw, intuitive drama.
there-will-be-blood.author: Stephanie Zacharek

there-will-be-blood.quote: Anderson almost brings off a picture worthy of his grandiose ambition.
there-will-be-blood.author: Mick LaSalle

there-will-be-blood.quote: Anderson and Day-Lewis strip themselves of their natural talents for invention and poetry, as if any hint of romance, nobility or fun would soften the film.
there-will-be-blood.author: Michael Sragow

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: This is an utterly absorbing film, a story that Scorsese sees as a secret history of American power, a hidden violence epidemic polluting the water table of humanity.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Peter Bradshaw

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: The three-and-a-half-hour running time is fully justified in an escalating tragedy that never loosens its grip — a sordid illustration of historical erasure with echoes in today’s bitterly divisive political gamesmanship.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: David Rooney

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Weaving the Tulsa race riots, the KKK and the Masons into its tapestry, Scorsese’s opus questions the misdeeds of America in the last century while linking them to the pressing issues of today. Addressing racial violence, nationalism, the continued epidemic of missing and murdered Indigenous women and even our lurid obsession with true crime, Killers of the Flower Moon paints a robust picture of a moment in history that invites viewer introspection.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Jane Crowther

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: On paper, this looks like a flatly impossible task for DiCaprio: the film’s central character is neither hero nor charismatic outlaw, but a grasping, biddable, determinedly unreflective stooge, whose actions inspire revulsion and outrage.But he meets the challenge with one of the finest, most complex performances he’s ever given.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Robbie Collin

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: DiCaprio and De Niro are brilliant, but it is relative unknown Lily Gladstone who is truly extraordinary.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Clarisse Loughrey

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Lifting his camera to survey the wide open plains of the past, Scorsese extracts an epic Western from horrible real-life crimes committed against the Native American Osage tribe of, latterly, Oklahoma, delivering something biblical, human, yet deeply inhumane.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Fionnuala Halligan

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Above all, it’s a Martin Scorsese picture, brimming with reverence for a culture that survived a horrible trauma as it is filled with exhilarating flourishes, film history references, and explorations of the faultline between the sacred and profane. And yes: It’s a masterpiece.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: David Fear

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: For all of the episodic ramble of Killers of the Flower Moon, not enough space is provided to restoring palpable personhood to people so relentlessly robbed of it.  Scorsese’s film is nonetheless effectively rattling, a grueling delineation of events that gracefully eschews the melodrama and sensationalism of so much true crime.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Richard Lawson

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: A tremendous but chilling achievement from one of America’s great storytellers.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: David Sims

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: The story’s romance is warmly inviting, and DiCaprio and Gladstone work beautifully together, their different performance styles — Ernest is physically demonstrative while Mollie is reserved — creating a contrapuntal whole.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Manohla Dargis

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers of the Flower Moon is monumentally long (206 minutes) and moves at an unhurried pace, but it knows where it’s going and barely a second is wasted. It’s sinuous and old-school, an instant American classic; almost Steinbeckian in its attention to detail and its banked, righteous rage.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Xan Brooks

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Serrated with political edge, Scorsese’s true-crime epic is impeccably constructed and utterly gripping.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Phil de Semlyen

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: It’s a heartbreaking story and all the more brutal for its surface-level simplicity.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Lou Thomas

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Monumental stuff: a story about the deadly legacy of America’s colonial sins, both vast and intimate in scope. Exceptional filmmaking, by an exceptional filmmaker.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: John Nugent

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Good old reliable Marty pulls it off again, addictively unraveling a tale that’s almost too terrible to be true with panache, gusto and just the right amount of cultural respect.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Johnny Oleksinski

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers of the Flower Moon is a cathedral of a movie, cavernously huge in ambition and scale, yet oddly intimate in its effect on the viewer.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Dana Stevens

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers of the Flower Moon is a three-hander on an epic canvas, a corrosive analysis of America’s colonialist and capitalist excesses as refracted through a marital melodrama in the vein of George Cukor’s Gaslight or Alfred Hitchcock’s Suspicion.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Keith Uhlich

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers of the Flower Moon is a three-hander on an epic canvas, a corrosive analysis of America’s colonialist and capitalist excesses as refracted through a marital melodrama in the vein of George Cukor’s Gaslight or Alfred Hitchcock’s Suspicion.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Keith Uhlich

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: This is a master artist putting a stamp on not only his own career, but also the entirety of American cinema and, why not, American history, too.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Barry Hertz

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: In the end, Killers of the Flower Moon is like a puzzle—each creative piece does its part to form the complete picture.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Brian Tallerico

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers Of The Flower Moon is as momentous as the country it’s set in and as full of history as the people whose murder it depicts.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Murtada Elfadl

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers of the Flower Moon is immeasurably captivating and compelling; it’s chilling and emotional, and I doubt anyone will walk away from the film — especially considering the way its ending is set up — without feeling moved by what they’ve just witnessed.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Mae Abdulbaki

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers of the Flower Moon earns its expansive presence. Not only is Scorsese trying to condense an epic of American history and true crime, its extravagant runtime emphasizes the staggering indifference — or, in some cases, deliberate neglect — by the Osage’s white neighbors to the acts of violence happening all around them, which allowed these crimes to continue for as long as they did.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Matt Singer

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: [Scorsese] has called his work an offering to the Osage, and to other Native peoples. It also feels like an offering to those who love cinema, allowing us to watch a master of the craft continue to force himself, unlikely as it seems, to stretch and learn. May he keep stretching — himself, and us.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Jocelyn Noveck

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: The villains are fairly obvious in “Flower Moon,” but Scorsese asks audiences to take a wider look at systemic racism, historical injustice and the corruptive influence of power and money, intriguingly tying together our past and present.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Brian Truitt

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: The result of all this careful questioning is stunning. To say Scorsese has made a great movie is to announce that water is wet, but there’s a kind of unfolding grief to Killers’ tone, a steady feeling of dread and sorrow, that only works in the hands of a master. You aren’t told how to feel so much as you’re made to feel it and then, in the end, be walloped with indignance over what happened to the story of the murders and many stories like them.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Alissa Wilkinson

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Martin Scorsese’s true-crime American period piece Killers of the Flower Moon is a big, sweeping, glorious, heartbreaking, insightful, powerful and unforgettable epic that serves notice the 80-year-old Scorsese remains at the forefront of innovative and provocative filmmaking.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Richard Roeper

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Out of a dark chapter of history about U.S. mistreatment of Native Americans, director Martin Scorsese crafts a new movie classic with stupendous acting from DiCaprio, DeNiro and newcomer Lily Gladstone. It's a great movie from our greatest filmmaker. See it now!
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Peter Travers

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: There’s a way of looking at this movie, a colossal tale of the sociopathy of American history, that’s a matter of listening to what’s said and what isn’t. The movie raises the idea of silence to a nearly transcendent pitch of passion.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Richard Brody

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers of the Flower Moon is vast and vital in its scale, purpose and emotional scope, a Western-thriller and ensemble piece that is every bit a Scorsese crime picture as one can dare to imagine.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Tomris Laffly

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Martin Scorsese triumphs yet again.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Luke Hicks

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: For all its extravagant running time (three hours and 26 minutes!), its big-swing history lessons, and its tale of an Old West giving way to the regimentation of a modern police force, Killers of the Flower Moon turns out to be that simplest and slipperiest of things: the story of a marriage. And a twisted, tragic one at that.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Bilge Ebiri

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers of the Flower Moon is a fast, fierce, and unapologetic gut punch that centers the horrific abuse suffered by the Osage nation at the hands of those who were entitled to nothing and thought themselves worthy of everything.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Lex Briscuso

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: It’s one of Scorsese’s most brutal films, yet one of his most thoughtful and self-reflexive, as he crafts a subversive murder “mystery” that leaves no lingering questions save for one.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Siddhant Adlakha

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers of the Flower Moon is a full-on cinematic experience. It’s rare that a movie that you should see is also one you want to see. This is one.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Bill Goodykoontz

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: “Killers” is a master class in filmmaking, taught by that one professor we all had in college whose every word we hung on, and whose classes always felt too short. It’s that thing we always look for but so rarely find: a great story, beautifully told.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Moira Macdonald

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Scorsese has rendered a tragic, forlorn piece of American history, indebted equally to classical Hollywood craftsmanship and the director’s own obsessions with honor, guilt, family, criminal codes and America’s centuries of greedy bloodshed.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Michael Phillips

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Roth and Scorsese carefully seed Killers of the Flower Moon’s script with context, texture, and detail, even when they’re avoiding exposition and making sure every scene has a dramatic point. It’s an incredibly lived-in movie.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Oli Welsh

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: In the end, I recommend seeing it, but I think Killers of the Flower Moon is the kind of movie you respect and admire without much actual enjoyment. With all the evident hard work, dedication and fidelity to facts, it’s still an hour too long and not a film I would ever want to see twice.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Rex Reed

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: This is epic filmmaking and a reminder that the kinds of antisocial, amoral characters who have long represented Scorsese’s bread-and-butter don’t exist exclusively on the mean streets of modern-day America.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: James Berardinelli

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Scorsese and cinematographer Rodrigo Prieto manage cinematic flourishes that tell us everything we need to know in a particular moment.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Josh Larsen

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: In his 80th year, Martin Scorsese remains a master of craft and storytelling, and while Killers of the Flower Moon may not rise to the greatest levels of his near-peerless canon, it’s still a more than worthy addition to his filmography.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Jason Gorber

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: It’s a difficult balancing act for a filmmaker as gifted and operatic as Scorsese, whose ability to tell any story rubs up against his ultimate admission that this might not be his story to tell. And so, for better or worse, Scorsese turns Killers of the Flower Moon into the kind of story that he can still tell better than anyone else: A story about greed, corruption, and the mottled soul of a country that was born from the belief that it belonged to anyone callous enough to take it.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: David Ehrlich

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Even amid its flaws — Scorsese’s sprawling focus leaving some characters in the dust, most of them the very indigenous Americans this film purports to speak for — Killers of the Flower Moon remains a staggering work of cinema.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Clint Worthington

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Scorsese is a master at his peak who has made deliberate choices about the story he wants to tell, and the way he wants to tell it, and he makes all of it count.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Karen Gordon

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: If “Killers” miscalibrates its balance of perspectives, it also discovers, in the luminous recesses of Gladstone’s performance, a quality of contemplation that beautifully suffuses and modulates Scorsese’s faster, more frenetic rhythms.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Justin Chang

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Those who do stick with Killers of the Flower Moon – and you all should – when it opens later in the year will, however, be rewarded with the most ingenious of closing codas. There are issues here, but the great man has still got it.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Donald Clarke

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: It is, it has to be said, something of a stretch to believe that this regal woman would be drawn to a dullard such as Ernest, but Gladstone and DiCaprio manage to convince us that this is more than a partnership of expediency – it’s a marriage of real love.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Wendy Ide

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: After the facile mysticism of Silence, the tone-deaf anti-union cant of The Irishman and the self-indulgent cutesiness of Rolling Thunder Revue: A Bob Dylan Story By Martin Scorsese, Killers of the Flower Moon feels like the work of a filmmaker who is doing more than just ticking off boxes on a decades-old wish list.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Richard Whittaker

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Bolstered by a strong cast and a luscious color palette and landscape, Killers of the Flower Moon is worthy of a watch for those who can look past its romanticization. For those looking for a film that puts Native American voices and characters on center stage or a more comprehensive story, continue moving on, even with three-and-a-half hours, this is not that film.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Therese Lacson

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: The Killers of the Flower Moon, a visceral epic, is the story of the wreckage of a people, the evil in white men’s hearts and the poison they spread, and the erasure that occurs when their stain touches you. It’s powerful, even when you’re left wondering if someone else could’ve spread the gospel.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Robert Daniels

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Martin Scorsese’s Killers of the Flower Moon is a bladder-buster of a movie with no obvious bathroom break, no section where the story starts to sag. This makes it, almost by definition, a good and admirable piece of work. But Killers of the Flower Moon is also a lumbering mess, an ungainly and tonally odd film that, for all the strength of its parts, has little cumulative impact.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Mick LaSalle

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: There’s no doubt that Killers of the Flower Moon reflects a shift in energy that is defensible — even necessary — from an ethical point of view. Narratively, that pivot results in a film that, it must be said, feels leeched of the energy and vigor viewers associate with Scorsese at his most exhilarating.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Ann Hornaday

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Killers of the Flower Moon is flawed, but still worth seeing. The film’s final scene, which will surely be divisive, is perhaps the best coda Scorsese’s ever shot and features his most intriguing cameo appearance. It’s a gutsy way to tie up all the film’s loose ends — proof that even this far in his career, he still has a few new tricks up his sleeve.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Odie Henderson

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Stylistically, this feels like a young man’s movie. It’s engrossing from the get-go, the palpable tension methodically echoed by Robbie Robertson’s steady-heartbeat score. But it keeps going and going until everyone we care about is dead, dying or behind bars, with nearly an hour still in store.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Peter Debruge

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Although its moral ambition is to honor the tribulations of an Indigenous people, it keeps getting pulled back into the orbit—emotional, social, and eventually legal—of white men.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Anthony Lane

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: An honorable try, the movie nevertheless doesn’t fully capture the enormity of the tragedy. At best it’s a sorrowful, necessary dirge. Other times, it’s like “Goodfellas” on the range but, understandably, without the spring-coiled momentum of that film.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Peter Rainer

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: This is on first impression perhaps a very good, uneven film rather than an unequivocally great one.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: David Jenkins

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: It’s a pity that on this occasion Scorsese makes an admirable and fine film, but alas not a great one.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: John Bleasdale

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: There’s a difference between “long” and “epic,” although in movie terms the two frequently get confused. Martin Scorsese delivers the former but not the latter with Killers of the Flower Moon.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Brian Lowry

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: I give Killers of the Flower Moon a mild recommendation. It’s too long and predictable. The saving grace is its performance across the board.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Alan Ng

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Most strikingly, for a murder thriller, Killers of the Flower Moon is fatally lacking in dread or suspense.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Stephen Dalton

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Scorsese has delivered an ordeal pretty much guaranteed to leave a bad taste in your mouth, one that in this case plays as pedestrian and repetitive, and never feels like an “epic.”
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Roger Moore

killers-of-the-flower-moon.quote: Ms. Gladstone draws a lot of sympathy as the modest, helpless Mollie, but like everything else here her performance suffers from inertia. She spends the bulk of the movie mired in illness and despondency, and her look mirrors how I felt as I watched: numb and trapped.
killers-of-the-flower-moon.author: Kyle Smith

eddington.quote: More conventional than any of Aster’s previous work, Eddington is also more rigorous and explicit in its political engagement — the work of a maturing filmmaker eager to make it clear that his dark and scathing sense of humor is anything but an empty provocation.
eddington.author: Elena Lazic

eddington.quote: Ari Aster’s Eddington is such a superb social satire about contemporary America that I want to bury it in the desert for 20 years. More distance will make it easier to laugh.
eddington.author: Amy Nicholson

eddington.quote: Aster, who’s exclusively interested in making the kind of films that should be reviewed straight onto a prescription pad, is too beholden to his neuroses for his latest movie to play like a cheap provocation. This time, however, there’s a good chance those are your neuroses, too.
eddington.author: David Ehrlich

eddington.quote: Aster packs a lot into the film but never loses control of the material. In his most mainstream work to date, he once again shows his mettle as a serious filmmaker.
eddington.author: Karen Gordon

eddington.quote: Your mileage will vary according to your stomach for this stuff, but I found myself breathless with giggles at times, sometimes the therapeutic laugh of recognition and sometimes because Aster has a keen eye for what’s most absurd about human nature.
eddington.author: Alissa Wilkinson

eddington.quote: Excoriating and exhilarating in equal measure, it is the first truly great movie to deal explicitly with the unique madness and malice that the global pandemic revealed, a kind of touchstone for a time and place that with only a few years remove feels at once as fictional and otherworldly as a sci-fi novel, and at the same time the very real-world harbinger of the political shifts that proceeded.
eddington.author: Jason Gorber

eddington.quote: The result is a magnificently off-the-rails poison pill of a film, one that skitters from paranoiac thriller to reactionary satire to something far more caustic and unnerving. It is the cinematic equivalent of long COVID – lingering, haunting, and demanding rigorous, skeptical investigation.
eddington.author: Barry Hertz

eddington.quote: Taking aim at the left, the right, and every mad thing in-between, it’s a fierce and funny provocation designed to p--- off everyone along the political spectrum.
eddington.author: Nick Schager

eddington.quote: Eddington isn’t a movie that moralizes, but at the same time it doesn’t take the stance that both sides make some good points. Rather it’s a period piece about recent history that articulates why everything feels so doomed right now while still finding the space to be utterly ridiculous.
eddington.author: Esther Zuckerman

eddington.quote: With Joaquin Phoenix at the height of his abilities, Eddington is, if you look close enough, just as, if not more terrifying than anything Paimon or a Swedish cult could ever unleash.
eddington.author: Emma Kiely

eddington.quote: Its low-level strangeness jumps to surreal and gory heights – and it keeps going higher until it hits a peak of gonzo high-adrenaline fun that leaves you reeling and breathless. Many viewers will have had enough of the film long before then, but there is something heroic about Aster's uncompromising determination to go his own way.
eddington.author: Nicholas Barber

eddington.quote: This is Aster’s funniest film to date, and makes use of an ever expanding and shifting cast to dot the 150-minute runtime with well-observed comic details and visual payoffs.
eddington.author: Sophie Monks Kaufman

eddington.quote: [Aster] wants to show us the really big picture, and while “Eddington” isn’t a horror movie, it puts its finger on a kind of madness you’ll recognize with a tremor.
eddington.author: Owen Gleiberman

eddington.quote: It's a film that never feels neutered or held back, and as such it lingers in the mind for days afterward.
eddington.author: Bill Bria

eddington.quote: An audacious, farcically funny digest of where we are now, and how we got here: the cinematic equivalent of pandemic primal therapy, a mad scream into the void.
eddington.author: John Nugent

eddington.quote: The film certainly is rare in actually offering an authentic depiction of social media and its noxious capabilities, even if its insistence on proving there’s no righteous moral that can’t be swiftly liquidated does become a little tiresome by the home stretch.
eddington.author: David Jenkins

eddington.quote: With its well-observed, often darkly hilarious details of oddball inhabitants and chilling deployment of the chaotic overwhelm of social media in our lives, Eddington walks a thin line between dread and comedy.
eddington.author: Christina Newland

eddington.quote: Is there too much going on? Possibly, but Eddington is never dull – Aster commits fully to his grisly vision of a ruptured America where a sticky narrative is more important than the truth or any kind of moral high ground.
eddington.author: Nick Levine

eddington.quote: Aster has always had a knack for confrontation, while Phoenix works best as an open-nerve. That the duo should prove so adept tapping into a vein of neurotic action is one of the many brutal surprises in a social satire as blunt and broad as America itself.
eddington.author: Ben Croll

eddington.quote: Eddington is especially pointed in the way that it views our online connectedness as a social cancer rather than an engine for progress.
eddington.author: Rocco T. Thompson

eddington.quote: Phoenix is the perfect instrument for Aster’s bleak and self-destructive view of humanity. Consider “Eddington” a warning.
eddington.author: G. Allen Johnson

eddington.quote: When Aster lays off the easy comic despair in favor of more ambiguous and dimensional feelings, interactions and moments, Eddington becomes the movie he wanted. His script has a million problems with clarity, coincidence and the nagging drag of a protagonist set up for a long, grisly comeuppance, yet Eddington is probably Aster’s strongest film visually.
eddington.author: Michael Phillips

eddington.quote: There are no safe places in his pictures. And Eddington is dense with multiple levels that stoke the ever-present unease.
eddington.author: Soren Andersen

eddington.quote: Opinions can range about whether Aster effectively captured this moment in time, or if this movie would have been more relevant if it had come out a few years earlier, when these memories were even fresher in our heads. But what feels both more important and undeniable is the intentionality with which he takes on this era, in all its ugliness.
eddington.author: Liz Shannon Miller

eddington.quote: Throughout human history, there has been something in our broken nature that resists community and seeks conflict. Eddington captures this, particularly the way it was fomented by the historical circumstances of 2020 America.
eddington.author: Josh Larsen

eddington.quote: The film never interrogates why the early pandemic led to so many ideological conflicts, but it suggests that the prognosis is bleak for those who continue to venture too far into the internet’s noxious rabbit holes. Being too online, in other words, can be its own kind of sickness.
eddington.author: Shirley Li

eddington.quote: The overall lack of subtlety suits the age Aster is taking to task, though it also makes everything feel slightly wobbly on its feet. The viewpoint is both-sides misanthropy. Jonathan Swift has some notes.
eddington.author: David Fear

eddington.quote: Eddington is only a partly coherent mishmash of tones and ideas: sincere and satirical, astute and self-obfuscating. The only thing it is completely is ambitious.
eddington.author: Farah Cheded

eddington.quote: It’s not just about the divisiveness of 2020; it’s designed to be divisive itself in 2025. To that end, even if you hate it, it’s kind of done its job.
eddington.author: Brian Tallerico

eddington.quote: Eddington gradually shifts away from the hyper topical and into a despairing, bleakly amusing look at an America prone to violent fantasy and deed, entrenched in escalating conflict, caught in a terrible entropy. When Aster finally knuckles down and ramps up the action, Eddington takes strange flight.
eddington.author: Richard Lawson

eddington.quote: No genre really makes more sense for this moment than horror — except, maybe, for black comedy, and Aster’s bracingly nasty but centerless new film offers plenty of both.
eddington.author: Alison Willmore

eddington.quote: If this wigged-out modern Western doesn’t quite work, it’s at the very least a cry of vexation over what our country, messy at the best of times, has become, thanks to a virus that found its way not just into our lungs, but into our very lifeblood. Dr. Aster has listened in on America’s heartbeat; the diagnosis is that we’re basically a mess.
eddington.author: Stephanie Zacharek

eddington.quote: At times, it can be bitterly hysterical, with Aster, who also wrote the film, further flexing his comedic muscles after his previous film with Phoenix. On the other hand, Eddington can be almost too on-the-nose, knicking the surface of complex issues but pulling the blade away before it can really draw blood.
eddington.author: Graeme Guttmann

eddington.quote: It’s a jumbled, intriguing, inconsistent mess — and yes, it is uncomfortable by design.
eddington.author: Bill Goodykoontz

eddington.quote: Full of sound and fury, signifying something. If only we knew what that was.
eddington.author: Tara Brady

eddington.quote: The character’s thinly sketched beliefs combined with Phoenix’s uncharacteristically vague performance keep him constantly at arm’s reach. We never really get into his head, which makes his eventual downfall (or Falling Down) feel both nihilistic and dramatically undercharged.
eddington.author: Rory O'Connor

eddington.quote: Eddington is a fascinating film whose high points are sure to grow in the public estimation with the distance of time, but whose murky themes and punishing runtime have more in common with advanced torture tactics than with traditional cinematic expression.
eddington.author: Dominic Griffin

eddington.quote: In certain moments, the film’s absurdism recalls that era’s paranoia and volcanic anger, but too often Aster overshoots the mark, collecting the period’s signature elements without finding much that is smart to say about them.
eddington.author: Tim Grierson

eddington.quote: Five years after we just went through (at least a lot of) this, “Eddington” somehow seems both too late and too soon, especially when it offers so little wisdom or insight beyond a vision of hopelessness.
eddington.author: Lindsey Bahr

eddington.quote: For all that “Eddington” variously concerns itself with politics and conspiracy theories and violence and the Western landscape, what it’s really about is social media.
eddington.author: Mark Feeney

eddington.quote: It’s kind of a mess, but an ambitious one hitting on themes Aster’s fans will recognize as his favorites. And as Aster scores points on conspiracy-obsessed America, cultish America, gun-fetishizing America, virtue signalling America and the limits of “back the blue,” he’s pretty much earned the right to be heard out, if not the benefit of the doubt.
eddington.author: Roger Moore

eddington.quote: Unfortunately, for all its button-pushing, the movie's biggest offense is that it is often tedious and meandering and it takes at least 30 minutes too long to cross the finish line.
eddington.author: James Berardinelli

eddington.quote: There is no accumulation of drama or tension or intellectual revelation and the setpiece shootout is ultimately valueless. What exactly is it saying that we didn’t know already? The wait for Aster to recover his directorial form goes on.
eddington.author: Peter Bradshaw

eddington.quote: It’s an ambitious contemporary western shot last year yet set in the summer of 2020, and ostensibly aims, in almost every scene, to analyse and ridicule the political obsessions and digital neuroses that dominated that moment. And, well, it’s quite the mess.
eddington.author: Kevin Maher

eddington.quote: It’s bloated, self-indulgent, rambling, crazily ambitious and commendably odd, but so overstuffed it becomes a lethal combination of baffling and boring.
eddington.author: David Rooney

eddington.quote: With Eddington, Ari Aster tries his hand at political satire and turns in his first bad movie.
eddington.author: Siddhant Adlakha

eddington.quote: Really, the problem with Eddington is not that Aster judges his characters. It’s that he barely finds them interesting enough to judge, and his boredom proves infectious.
eddington.author: Justin Chang

eddington.quote: Aster is so intent on using ripped-from-the-headlines events that he fails to make proper use of them, and ends up cynically debasing them all.
eddington.author: Richard Brody

eddington.quote: For a movie drenched in foreboding in menace, there’s very little narrative tension in “Eddington,” a problem Aster solves with an intrusive sound design and dissonant, clanging piano chords.
eddington.author: Ann Hornaday

eddington.quote: America undoubtedly needs serious artists to explore the brain worms that the pandemic era gave the body politic, but Eddington most definitely ain’t it.
eddington.author: Richard Whittaker

mickey-17.quote: For all the cruelty and buffoonery that might surround his hero, Bong lets us in on a revelation: what we’re really watching is a man learning that it’s OK for him to be happy.
mickey-17.author: Clarisse Loughrey

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17 is funny and charming from the get-go, building out a fascinating sci-fi world from its central conceit that ends up speaking to powerful and timely concerns through humour, satire and exhilarating genre elements. Bong Joon-ho's best English movie to date and arguably Robert Pattinson's best movie ever.
mickey-17.author: David Opie

mickey-17.quote: Bong keeps things zipping along, and with such nimbleness that the movie’s heavier ideas never weigh it down. He jabs rather than pounds as he takes on targets — authoritarianism, comic-book heroics, the vanity of power — while playfully mixing moods and acting styles.
mickey-17.author: Manohla Dargis

mickey-17.quote: This isn’t just another great Bong Joon Ho movie about how much he hates capitalism (though it definitely is that too), it’s the first Bong Joon Ho movie about how much he loves people.
mickey-17.author: David Ehrlich

mickey-17.quote: The entire spectacle is so unabashedly outrageous that you cannot help but side with its many excesses.
mickey-17.author: Barry Hertz

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17 is a long ride with a running time of about two hours and twenty minutes, with unexpected twists and turns. It’s a lot of fun, and as previously noted, is stuffed with ideas.
mickey-17.author: Karen Gordon

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17 crystalizes our horrific reality into an existential parable, one that fundamentally understands the hell of working-class existence with the allegorical precision of "The Twilight Zone." It's a story about people finding love, connection, and community under hopeless circumstances, and a rallying cry that we all deserve better conditions for existing.
mickey-17.author: BJ Colangelo

mickey-17.quote: Above all, Mickey 17 is remarkable for the savagery of its satire of 21st-century capitalism.
mickey-17.author: Dana Stevens

mickey-17.quote: Pattinson is fully committed to the performance – performances – and his impact subtly evolves from giggling to genuinely moving. That same evolution applies to the whole of Bong’s film, which dances so close to the edge of grand folly, the effect is exhilarating.
mickey-17.author: Kimberley Jones

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17 may not be my preferred mode of Bong Joon-Ho, but it’s the mode we need right now.
mickey-17.author: Josh Larsen

mickey-17.quote: If Mickey’s life is suffocatingly bleak, Mickey 17 is anything but. Rather, it’s a wacky, satisfyingly strange romp that further reaffirms Bong Joon Ho as a singular filmmaker.
mickey-17.author: Shirley Li

mickey-17.quote: Bong succinctly riffs on old Hollywood to maintain his legacy of class-conscious films that challenge the status quo appealingly and refreshingly.
mickey-17.author: Digby Houghton

mickey-17.quote: Bong specializes in crushing capitalist dystopias, whether he’s skewering present-day South Korea or an even more stratified post-apocalyptic society, and the near-future in which Mickey 17 takes place is perverse enough for each detail to constitute its own dark joke.
mickey-17.author: Alison Willmore

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17, about a hapless clone’s misadventures on a colonising mission, is a throwback to blockbusters as the late 20th century made ’em: a $100m boisterous sci-fi satire that neither belongs to a franchise nor cares to start one, but instead jams as many eggs as it can into one increasingly precarious basket.
mickey-17.author: Robbie Collin

mickey-17.quote: Like Mickey himself, it’s goofy and a little inconsistent, but it’s also funny, thoughtful and more plausible than we might like. A charming space oddity for these unusual times.
mickey-17.author: Helen O'Hara

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17 may lack some of the political bite of his previous work – though there are Trumpian elements in Marshall – but it’s unquestionably tremendous fun: a big, strange spectacle that’s unlike most blockbuster cinema out there.
mickey-17.author: Lou Thomas

mickey-17.quote: He may have developed, produced and directed just one movie — this boisterous Robert Pattinson sci-fi comedy — but, yikes, has he packed a lot into Mickey 17.
mickey-17.author: Kevin Maher

mickey-17.quote: A deeply depressing comedic experience (thanks at least in part to accidental political timing), Bong’s remix of Edward Ashton’s novel presents a Trump-like villain and no worthy heroes, resulting in a farcical sci-fi adventure whose symbolism makes up for its misshapen character drama.
mickey-17.author: Siddhant Adlakha

mickey-17.quote: Director Bong returns to familiar territory, but with no less ambition or heart than he has shown throughout his career.
mickey-17.author: Hannah Strong

mickey-17.quote: Even if DNA and memories could be duplicated at will, Bong suggests, individual morality would remain a glorious uncertainty principle, too human and singular to be nailed down. There’s a strange comfort in that idea, and in the movie’s sweetly hopeful finale.
mickey-17.author: Justin Chang

mickey-17.quote: Bong has some cache to make whatever he wants, and he uses this freedom to build a wild and intriguing world that is both humorous and politically charged.
mickey-17.author: Ross Bonaime

mickey-17.quote: There’s an infectious warmth to proceedings that makes you stick with Mickey 17 (and 18) through thick and thin. This kooky curio is well worth seeking out.
mickey-17.author: Nick Levine

mickey-17.quote: Balanced with the over-the-top but spot-on performances by Ruffalo and Collette as the clear “rich guy turned politician that has a really really loyal fanbase” stand-in, "Mickey 17" is one of Bong’s best English-language films.
mickey-17.author: Amanda Luberto

mickey-17.quote: That exquisite balance of art and entertainment is exactly what makes each Bong Joon-ho film a gift to be savored – here's hoping his next one doesn't take quite so long to reach us.
mickey-17.author: Alexander Harrison

mickey-17.quote: Repeating his historic Oscar wins for Parasite is off the table for Bong Joon-ho. It's not happening. But together with his up-for-anything star Robert Pattinson in multiple roles, Bong turns this scattershot sci-fi space opera into a buoyant social satire that really stings
mickey-17.author: Peter Travers

mickey-17.quote: A Bong Joon-ho film for the fans of 'Okja' and 'Snowpiercer'. Our generation's liveliest, most earnest director is back.
mickey-17.author: Francisca Tinoco

mickey-17.quote: While Mickey 17 isn’t in the same elevated league as Parasite, it’s a lot of fun.
mickey-17.author: Wendy Ide

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17 is a highly entertaining absurdist ride that embraces nihilism right up until the moment it tenderly skewers it.
mickey-17.author: Francesca Steele

mickey-17.quote: The film, in short, exhilarates and exhausts in equal measure, abundant in ambition and arduous, at points, in execution. And after six long years of waiting, one can hardly fault a bit of excess generosity – even if the feast leaves you stuffed if not quite satisfied.
mickey-17.author: Ben Croll

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17 is in no way a revolutionary follow up to something like 2019’s Parasite, but it’s an entertaining, well crafted ride.
mickey-17.author: Katarina Docalovich

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17 is at its best when director Bong really leans into exploring the dirty details of blue-collar space exploration.
mickey-17.author: Liz Shannon Miller

mickey-17.quote: Though Mickey 17 can feel like a mixtape of Bong’s greatest hits, it may actually be his most refined and articulate anti-capitalistic critique to date.
mickey-17.author: Rocco T. Thompson

mickey-17.quote: Bong covered many of the same aspects of “Mickey” in his 2013 sci-fi epic “Snowpiercer,” a more streamlined and hard-bitten work of social commentary with the have-nots battling the heedless rich. ”Mickey 17” is less focused and not quite as satisfying a production as that earlier movie.
mickey-17.author: Soren Andersen

mickey-17.quote: It’s a variation on the teletransportation paradox as filtered through a live-action Looney Tunes cartoon, with some B-movie creatures thrown in for good measure.
mickey-17.author: Richard Roeper

mickey-17.quote: Comparisons aside, Mickey 17 is a remarkably solid and compelling sci-fi flick, with an absurdist flair that can only come from a filmmaker like Joon Ho.
mickey-17.author: Emily Zemler

mickey-17.quote: Bong has an original vision and a distinctive style that’s not to be dismissed. He’s our era’s Terry Gilliam, where hope pushes through the tragicomic nihilism.
mickey-17.author: G. Allen Johnson

mickey-17.quote: Messy as it is, the filmmaking so energetically delivers its acidic pessimism that it’s rarely unpleasant.
mickey-17.author: Jacob Oller

mickey-17.quote: If this is Bong’s take on a Hollywood space blockbuster, it’s better than most. “Mickey 17,” led by a quirky underdog, offers a timely escape where empathy can overcome cruelty on the other side of the galaxy.
mickey-17.author: Brian Truitt

mickey-17.quote: It’s [Bong Joon Ho's] first film since “Parasite” became the first foreign language movie to win a best picture Oscar in 2020, and while it’s not his best work, “Mickey 17” is still a great deal of acrid fun. In the bargain, you get three great performances from two very good actors.
mickey-17.author: Ty Burr

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17 sometimes wobbles balancing its different tones. But what holds Bong’s eighth feature together is his palpable rage at humanity’s cruelty mixed with his compassion for a protagonist who cannot die – and, therefore, cannot truly live.
mickey-17.author: Tim Grierson

mickey-17.quote: As semi-inessential as Mickey 17 feels in Bong’s canon, I’m at peace that he keeps asking how to give everyone’s life value. He’ll keep repeating the question until we come up with an answer.
mickey-17.author: Amy Nicholson

mickey-17.quote: What’s frustrating is that I totally agree with everything Bong is saying, I just wish he were saying it with a touch more finesse. Maybe they can do some fine-tuning in the lab for next time.
mickey-17.author: Christy Lemire

mickey-17.quote: Even a first-rate director can get a little lost in the tone management and narrative streamlining process.
mickey-17.author: Michael Phillips

mickey-17.quote: If the movies are going to talk about labor, human rights, cruel “leaders” and love in the world Gen Z is growing up in, the raw deal facing Mickeys 1-17 is a good place to do it.
mickey-17.author: Roger Moore

mickey-17.quote: It’s eerie, startling — and yet also unexpectedly benign.
mickey-17.author: Peter Bradshaw

mickey-17.quote: Bong’s adventurous new film barrels forward with chaotic plotting, as is often the case with the director’s work. But thematic coherence remains frustratingly elusive.
mickey-17.author: David Rooney

mickey-17.quote: It's the weakest of his three English language efforts due to it feeling like he's watering down his satirical approach, spoon-feeding exposition to his audience alongside each joke under the worry that the parody might go over their heads.
mickey-17.author: Alistair Ryder

mickey-17.quote: No matter a committed performance (two, actually) from Robert Pattinson, it’s an original that plays like a rehash—and an underwhelmingly unfunny one at that.
mickey-17.author: Nick Schager

mickey-17.quote: Bong is a consummate cinematic craftsman, virtually incapable of creating a dull frame. What’s happening within those impeccable compositions, however, feels like its suffering from an overabundance of business and undernourished storytelling.
mickey-17.author: David Fear

mickey-17.quote: Though it earns points for sheer oddity (and the nearly monochromatic, future-noir look established by DP Darius Khondji and production designer Fiona Crombie), too much of “Mickey 17” turns out to be sloppy, shrill and preachy — ironically, the same things that make Mark Ruffalo’s deliberately Trump-styled villain so grating in this movie.
mickey-17.author: Peter Debruge

mickey-17.quote: In an extremely physical, committed, even exhausting performance, Pattinson takes what could have been an unwieldy mess and makes it much less, well, expendable.
mickey-17.author: Jocelyn Noveck

mickey-17.quote: While the visuals are often stunning, and the first hour has a loose, raunchy charm, “Mickey 17″ wears out its welcome long before its overlong, nearly t2½-hour runtime ends.
mickey-17.author: Odie Henderson

mickey-17.quote: It’s far from terrible and a pleasure to look at. But, perhaps inevitably, after such a raging success, Bong’s latest movie is a disappointment.
mickey-17.author: Johnny Oleksinski

mickey-17.quote: A mostly failed attempt to merge sci-fi with satire, Mickey 17 suffers from a fragmented narrative and a scenery-chewing performance from Mark Ruffalo that belongs in a different movie (perhaps Poor Things).
mickey-17.author: James Berardinelli

mickey-17.quote: While Bong Joon Ho delivers his signature visual flair and Robert Pattinson fully commits to the existential dread of his endlessly disposable character, the film struggles to keep its high-concept ideas fresh past the first act.
mickey-17.author: Alan Ng

mickey-17.quote: On the whole, though, Mickey 17 tests our patience. While the dispensable clones premise is intriguing, and opens a door to the kind of socioeconomic commentary so signature to Bong, the film quickly grows distracted by other matters entirely.
mickey-17.author: Richard Lawson

mickey-17.quote: Again and again lines and scenes strain for comic effect, but fail to deliver the goods.
mickey-17.author: Hugh Montgomery

mickey-17.quote: Mickey 17, adapted from a novel by Edward Ashton, feels like a rickety compromise bolted together from incompatible parts.
mickey-17.author: Donald Clarke

mickey-17.quote: The time may feel right for a wry dystopian sci-fi adventure-comedy. But as satires go, this one is more mild than habanero.
mickey-17.author: Stephanie Zacharek

mickey-17.quote: Even an audience expecting very little would be underwhelmed by this meandering, snowy dud, which, for all its extravagance, at a reported $120 million budget, combines insipid messaging with witless comedy and a weak plot that gets resolved in a silly way.
mickey-17.author: Kyle Smith

the-social-network.quote: With a thieves den of borderline-Shakespearian characters, a wickedly literate screenplay, potent direction by David Fincher, an exceptional ensemble cast and subject matter that speaks to a generation and well beyond, The Social Network is mesmerizing.
the-social-network.author: Pete Hammond

the-social-network.quote: Keep your eyes on Garfield - he's shatteringly good, the soul of a film that might otherwise be without one. The Social Network is the movie of the year. But Fincher and Sorkin triumph by taking it further. Lacing their scathing wit with an aching sadness, they define the dark irony of the past decade.
the-social-network.author: Peter Travers

the-social-network.quote: The film comes down to a mesmerizing portrait of a man who in any other age would perhaps be deemed nuts or useless, but in the Internet age has this mental agility to transform an idea into an empire.
the-social-network.author: Kirk Honeycutt

the-social-network.quote: Continues Fincher's fascinating transition from genre filmmaker extraordinaire to indelible chronicler of our times.
the-social-network.author: Justin Chang

the-social-network.quote: Quite possibly the first truly great fact-based movie of the 21st century.
the-social-network.author: Lou Lumenick

the-social-network.quote: It's a grandly entertaining reminder of everything we used to go to the movies for (and still can't get online): sparkling dialogue, thorny situations, soulful performances, and an unusually open-ended and relevant engagement with a major social issue of the day: how we (dis)connect.
the-social-network.author: Joshua Rothkopf

the-social-network.quote: Brilliantly entertaining and emotionally wrenching.
the-social-network.author: David Denby

the-social-network.quote: The rewards for paying attention are mammoth and exhilarating. This is a high-IQ movie that gives viewers an IQ high.
the-social-network.author: Richard Corliss

the-social-network.quote: The power of The Social Network is that Zuckerberg is a weasel with a mission that can never be dismissed. The movie suggests that he may have built his ambivalence about human connection into Facebook's very DNA. That's what makes him a jerk-hero for our time.
the-social-network.author: Owen Gleiberman

the-social-network.quote: It's one of the best movies of the year, one of the best entries ever in the Way We Live Now oeuvre.
the-social-network.author: Bill Goodykoontz

the-social-network.quote: On the level of craft, the movie's just absurdly enjoyable. Sorkin's dialogue dazzles; the photography is burnished and sleek; the editing confidently sorts out a complex narrative.
the-social-network.author: Ty Burr

the-social-network.quote: The performances, direction and writing of one of the best pictures of 2010 make this Social Network every bit as addictive, and a little chilling as well.
the-social-network.author: Roger Moore

the-social-network.quote: This is a remarkable film for more reasons than its antihero, from the cyberspeed wisdom of Aaron Sorkin's screenplay to Jeff Cronenweth's camera prowling the excesses of youthful genius gone wild.
the-social-network.author: Steve Persall

the-social-network.quote: David Fincher's film has the rare quality of being not only as smart as its brilliant hero, but in the same way. It is cocksure, impatient, cold, exciting and instinctively perceptive.
the-social-network.author: Roger Ebert

the-social-network.quote: Smartly written by Aaron Sorkin, directed to within an inch of its life by David Fincher and anchored by a perfectly pitched performance by Jesse Eisenberg, The Social Network is a barn-burner of a tale that unfolds at a splendid clip.
the-social-network.author: Kenneth Turan

the-social-network.quote: Delivers the heady, rib-tickling rush of an action picture, and it gradually builds to an emotional wallop that blindsides you.
the-social-network.author: Rene Rodriguez

the-social-network.quote: The film owes much of its success to the inspired pairing of Fincher and Sorkin.
the-social-network.author: Claudia Puig

the-social-network.quote: The founding of Facebook becomes a tale for our times in this masterful social drama.
the-social-network.author: J.R. Jones

the-social-network.quote: David Fincher obsesses about obsessive people.
the-social-network.author: Lawrence Toppman

the-social-network.quote: Most of all, it is the improbably entertaining story of how new media are altering the very nature of courtship and friendship.
the-social-network.author: Carrie Rickey

the-social-network.quote: A work deeper than its nickname, "The Facebook Movie," hints at - coils around your brain. Weeks after seeing it, moments from it will haunt you.
the-social-network.author: Joe Neumaier

the-social-network.quote: A film that's at once timely and timeless.
the-social-network.author: Calvin Wilson

the-social-network.quote: Terrific entertainment - an unlikely thriller that makes business ethics, class distinctions and intellectual-property arguments sexy, that zips through two hours quicker than you can say "relationship status," and that'll likely fascinate pretty much anyone not named Zuckerberg.
the-social-network.author: Bob Mondello

the-social-network.quote: The Social Network has understandably been compared to "Citizen Kane" in its depiction of a man who changes society through bending an emergent technology to his will.
the-social-network.author: Ann Hornaday

the-social-network.quote: This account of Facebook's founder, and of the website's explosive growth, quickly lifts you to a state of exhilaration, and pretty much keeps you there for two hours.
the-social-network.author: Joe Morgenstern

the-social-network.quote: Shot to shot, scene to scene, The Social Network nearly never puts a foot wrong or, really, does anything to make you feel less than compelled.
the-social-network.author: Shawn Levy

the-social-network.quote: But make no mistake, whether the movie is fair or horribly unfair - I know nothing of the actual facts and can't make that determination - its portrait of Zuckerberg is a hatchet job of epic and perhaps lasting proportions.
the-social-network.author: Mick LaSalle

the-social-network.quote: The result is a ripped-from-the-Zeitgeist film that is razor-sharp, an astute and funny portrait of the early 2000s, with all its LOL's, its IMO's and its WTF's. Mostly its WTF's.
the-social-network.author: Mike Scott

the-social-network.quote: Fincher and his screenwriter, TV writer-god Aaron Sorkin, have made a seemingly modest picture that achieves something close to greatness the old-fashioned, slow-burning way: By telling a story with faces, dialogue and body language of all types, from awkward to swaggering.
the-social-network.author: Stephanie Zacharek

the-social-network.quote: Zuckerberg's story ends up feeling bigger than his own life.
the-social-network.author: Keith Phipps

the-social-network.quote: When Mr. Eisenberg makes Mark's face go blank, the character seems scarily emptied out: it's a subtly great, at times unsettling, performance.
the-social-network.author: Manohla Dargis

the-social-network.quote: All I can say about Timberlake's performance as the thoroughly odious, desperately seductive, textbook-case metrosexual Parker is that he brings so much reptilian fun that he unbalances the movie, almost fatally.
the-social-network.author: Andrew O'Hehir

the-social-network.quote: Blisteringly entertaining.
the-social-network.author: Kimberley Jones

the-social-network.quote: Is director David Fincher's film the stuff of greatness? Not quite. But the picture is very, very good.
the-social-network.author: Michael Phillips

the-social-network.quote: It has the staccato wit of a drawing-room comedy, the fatal flaw of a tragic romance and the buzzy immediacy of a front-page headline, all powered by a kinetic engine typically found in an action flick. And that's just the opening scene.
the-social-network.author: Rick Groen

the-social-network.quote: Eisenberg, one of those young actors who has existed just below the radar for several years now (he was the lead in both "Zombieland" and "Adventureland," not to be confused with one another), deserves an Oscar for this dead-on portrayal of a temperamental genius.
